title: Orbit and Signal
premise: Cyrus Whitlock, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Meridian, has spent nine years maintaining the silent routes between abandoned colonies. When a distress signal arrives in Vessari — a language extinct for two centuries, the tongue of his late wife's people — he decodes a plea from a hidden settlement of survivors that the colonial authority long declared dead. Racing a failing reactor's countdown and an authority warship sent to erase the signal's source, Cyrus must reach the edge-of-dead-space relay and rebroadcast the truth to every world still listening. He succeeds at the cost of his station and nearly his life, choosing justice outside the law over the duty that kept him alone.
about_author: Elodie Nystrom is a former radio engineer who spent a decade calibrating deep-space communication arrays before turning to fiction. She writes about lonely signals, stubborn machines, and the people who refuse to stop listening.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Cyrus runs his maintenance circuit through the dead relay chain, talking to the automated stations because no one else answers. His POV establishes his isolation, his grief for his Vessari wife Sefa, and the quiet dignity of his routine. Emotional beat: loneliness worn smooth into habit.

chapters.title: A Voice in Extinct Tongues
chapters.summary: At relay Kestrel-9, an impossible signal arrives: Vessari, a language officially extinct. Cyrus, half-fluent from his marriage, recognizes a distress pattern beneath the static. His POV; wonder curdles into dread as he realizes someone is alive who shouldn't be. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by hope.

chapters.title: What the Authority Buried
chapters.summary: Cyrus digs through sealed archives and finds the Vessari Purge records redacted beyond recognition. Flashbacks to Sefa's stories of her homeworld. His POV. Emotional beat: the slow realization that his employers built the silence he lives in.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Dark
chapters.summary: Meridian's aging reactor begins an uncommanded shutdown sequence — ninety days to total failure, no replacement parts ever coming again. Cyrus must choose: evacuate on the next supply skiff or stay. His POV. Emotional beat: duty as a cage he suddenly sees the bars of.

chapters.title: The Passenger
chapters.summary: A damaged authority courier docks unannounced carrying Ilsa Vane, a disgraced signal-integrity auditor who flagged the same anomaly and was silenced. Dual tension between them; her POV reveals the authority's cover-up machinery. Emotional beat: two strangers testing whether trust is survivable.

chapters.title: Decoding Sefa
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Ilsa work the translation together; the signal resolves into coordinates in dead space and a name — Ashfall, a settlement thought vaporized. Cyrus hears echoes of Sefa's lullabies in the phrasing. Alternating POV. Emotional beat: intimacy rebuilt out of shared purpose.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, One Ship
chapters.summary: They strip Meridian's systems to keep the reactor limping while fitting the ancient tug Perihelion for the run to dead space. Ilsa proposes broadcasting everything; Cyrus hesitates — it means treason. His POV. Emotional beat: love against duty, argued across a workbench.

chapters.title: The Hunter Class
chapters.summary: An authority warship, Vigilant, enters the sector hunting the signal leak. Its captain, Ondrey Marsh, is methodical and genuinely believes erasure prevents war. Marsh's POV gives the antagonist humanity. Emotional beat: conviction as its own kind of blindness.

chapters.title: Departure Without Clearance
chapters.summary: Cyrus launches the Perihelion minutes before Vigilant's boarding party arrives, leaving Meridian running on fumes as a decoy beacon. Escape sequence; near-capture in the debris fields. His POV. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into exhilaration — first choice he's made in years.

chapters.title: Static Between Stars
chapters.summary: The long transit through dead space; systems fail one by one. Ilsa confesses she once signed off on a suppression order before understanding what it meant. Her POV. Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution and not finding cheap grace.

chapters.title: Ashfall
chapters.summary: They reach the coordinates: a hollowed moon sheltering eleven thousand Vessari survivors, descendants of those the purge missed. Elder Maren Kesh greets them with wary hospitality. Shared POV. Emotional beat: awe and shame — Cyrus walks among ghosts who are alive.

chapters.title: The Children of the Signal
chapters.summary: Ashfall's story unfolds: generations underground, their transmitter their only voice, sending pleas for decades into a network designed not to hear. Maren shows Cyrus Sefa's family name among their records. His POV. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into belonging.

chapters.title: Vigilant Closes
chapters.summary: Marsh traces the decoy trail and burns toward Ashfall with orders to sterilize the signal source. His second-in-command begins questioning the mission. Marsh's POV. Emotional beat: the antagonist's certainty starting to fissure.

chapters.title: The Edge Relay
chapters.summary: The only transmitter powerful enough to reach inhabited space is Terminus, the derelict relay at the edge of dead space — dead for forty years, reachable only through a radiation corridor. Cyrus volunteers; Ilsa insists on coming. Planning chapter. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Corridor of Fire
chapters.summary: The run through the radiation belt; the Perihelion's shielding fails progressively, Ilsa burned and injured keeping the engines alive. His POV. Emotional beat: love expressed as refusal to leave each other behind.

chapters.title: Terminus
chapters.summary: They board the frozen relay and begin hand-reviving its fusion plant while the countdown clock on Meridian — now their only warning system — ticks toward zero. His POV, feverish and intimate. Emotional beat: two people building a heartbeat for a dead machine.

chapters.title: Marsh's Choice
chapters.summary: Vigilant arrives at Ashfall to find civilians, not insurgents. Maren refuses to hide; children stand in the open. Marsh's second-in-command mutinies verbally; Marsh stalls his own strike window. His POV. Emotional beat: conscience overtaking orders.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Terminus ignites. Cyrus transmits the full record — the purge archives, Ashfall's testimony, the intercepted orders — to every receiver in the network, then keys in a final message in Vessari: Sefa's lullaby, sung back to her people. His POV. Emotional beat: catharsis; the silence broken forever.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Vigilant receives the broadcast mid-approach. Marsh stands down, arrests his own mission log, and turns his ship to shield Ashfall instead. The authority's command fractures publicly. Marsh's POV. Emotional beat: justice achieved not by force but by truth arriving on time.

chapters.title: Meridian's Last Light
chapters.summary: The reactor countdown reaches zero; Meridian dies gloriously on the horizon of Cyrus's old life, its final automated message a farewell he wrote himself years ago. He watches from Terminus. His POV. Emotional beat: mourning the cage even as it falls.

chapters.title: Orbit and Signal
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the colonies respond, ships come, the law scrambles to catch up with what everyone now knows. Cyrus, recovering, is offered medals and tribunals and declines both. Ilsa stays. His POV. Emotional beat: quiet after the storm, love chosen freely at last.

chapters.title: The First Answer
chapters.summary: From Ashfall's restored tower, Cyrus helps train a new generation of listeners. A reply arrives from a colony no one knew survived — in another old language, asking simply: is anyone there? He answers yes. His POV closes the book. Emotional beat: hope as ongoing work, never finished.
